briefing.fuel: Fuel it: carbs beforehand, then practice race-day intake — a gel every ~25-30min and sips of fluid. The gut is trainable; race day is not the day to find out.

weeks.intro: Peak week 1 of 2: converting fitness to race-readiness — race-pace work dominates and sessions look like the race. 3 weeks to race day.

workouts.name: 12 x 200m Speed Reps
workouts.description: Short, fast repetitions developing speed and running economy. Full recovery between reps.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Shortest, fastest reps of the plan — your cadence has sat low (150-160 spm) all block, so this is the best remaining chance to bank some genuinely quick turnover before the taper starts.

briefing.purpose: Speed and running economy — short, fast reps recruit fast-twitch fibres and sharpen form, making every slower pace cheaper.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 12× (200m fast & relaxed — mile race effort @ 3:30-3:45/km / 60s walking rest @ 4:35-5:03/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km
briefing.feel: Fast, springy and light — ~95%, never an all-out sprint. Full recovery is part of the design; R work only counts when you're fresh for each rep.
briefing.if_wrong: Form breaking (shoulders up, overstriding)? Stop the set — junk reps train junk form. These reps are about quality, never volume.
briefing.warmup: After the easy warm-up: 2-3 drills (high knees, A-skips) plus 2-3 strides — fast reps on a cold engine is how calves tear.
briefing.cue: Think 'fast feet on hot coals' — ground contact short, heels never settling.
briefing.venue: Track or a measured flat stretch — GPS pace lies over 200-400m, so run these by effort and check splits after.

workouts.name: 4km Easy + 6 Strides
workouts.description: Easy run finishing with short strides to develop running economy and neuromuscular coordination.
workouts.notes: Cadence check-in one more time before taper — the fresher legs from reduced cross-training volume (if you've been able to dial that back) should make quick strides feel easier than earlier in the block.

briefing.purpose: Easy volume plus neuromuscular priming — strides teach fast, relaxed turnover without fatigue, and set up the next quality day.
briefing.structure: 3.2 km easy @ 4:35-5:03/km → 6× (Stride — fast & relaxed @ 3:30-3:45/km / 45s walking rest @ 4:35-5:03/km)
briefing.feel: Easy throughout; strides are fast and springy, ~90% effort, never sprinted.
briefing.if_wrong: Strides feeling forced or heavy-legged? Cut them — the easy running is the session; strides are a bonus.
briefing.cue: Strides are turnover practice: quick light steps, arms driving straight back, eyes up.

workouts.name: 4 x 1.0km Race Pace Intervals
workouts.description: Race-specific intervals at race pace. Builds confidence and specificity.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Race-pace intervals this close to race day are about confidence, not fitness — if these feel comfortable relative to week 5's marathon-pace segments, that's the signal the plan is working.

briefing.purpose: Race specificity — goal pace becomes automatic through repetition. Rhythm, relaxation and confidence at the pace that matters.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 4× (1.0 km at race pace @ 4:16-4:32/km / 90s walking rest @ 4:35-5:03/km) → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km
briefing.feel: Should feel 'sustainably quick' — if it feels like a fight now, the goal needs re-examining (that's useful information, not failure).
briefing.if_wrong: Consistently outside the window at honest effort: log it — the adaptive review uses exactly this signal to adjust your paces.

workouts.name: 11km Long Run w/ 3km Race Pace
workouts.description: Long run with a sustained race-pace block to build specificity and confidence.

steps.description: 15 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Final long run before taper, and your biggest at 11km — respect that this is new distance for you given a 13.5km/week baseline, so the 3km race-pace close should feel controlled, not maximal.

briefing.purpose: Race specificity — goal pace on tired legs, plus a dress rehearsal for pacing, fueling and kit.
briefing.structure: 15 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 3.3 km easy @ 4:35-5:03/km → 3 km at race pace @ 4:16-4:32/km → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km
briefing.feel: Race-pace block should feel controlled and rhythmic, not desperate — lock in after 1km and relax into it.
briefing.if_wrong: Can't hold the window without straining? Shorten the block rather than slowing the whole run — quality of pace beats quantity today.
briefing.fuel: Fuel it: carbs beforehand, then practice race-day intake — a gel every ~25-30min and sips of fluid. The gut is trainable; race day is not the day to find out.

workouts.name: 2km Easy Run
workouts.description: Relaxed aerobic run at conversational pace. Builds base fitness.
workouts.notes: Volume is deliberately low now — if your HYROX/cardio classes are still running near-daily, this is the week to trim those back too; the plan can't do that for you.

briefing.purpose: Aerobic base — most of your fitness is built here, at an effort that lets you absorb the hard days instead of digging the hole deeper.
briefing.feel: Conversational, RPE 3-4. You should finish feeling like you could do it again.
briefing.if_wrong: If pace drifts above the window to hold a conversation, let it — easy means effort, not a number. Heart rate above ~75% max: slow down.
briefing.cue: Cadence: count 30 right-foot strikes in 20s (target creeping up over the plan) — quicker, shorter steps, no overstriding.

workouts.name: 4km Tempo Run
workouts.description: Sustained threshold-pace effort. Develops lactate clearance and mental focus.

steps.description: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace

workouts.notes: Last tempo effort before race week — it should feel clearly easier than week 1's, at the same pace window; that comparison is your best fitness readout.

briefing.purpose: Lactate threshold — raises the pace you can sustain. The single biggest lever for Taper-phase fitness at your distance.
briefing.structure: 10 min easy jog at conversational pace @ 4:35-5:03/km → 4 km tempo at threshold pace @ 4:04-4:18/km → 10 min easy jog to finish @ 4:35-5:03/km
briefing.feel: Comfortably hard, RPE 7. You could speak a sentence, not hold a chat.
briefing.if_wrong: Too hard? Slow 5-10 s/km rather than stopping — the aerobic stimulus survives a slower tempo, not a broken one. Heat or hills: switch to effort.
briefing.cue: Lock the rhythm with your breathing (e.g. 2:2) and let pace follow it.

workouts.name: 7km Long Run
workouts.description: Steady long run building endurance and mental toughness at easy pace.
workouts.notes: Last long run before race week — shorter than recent long runs on purpose, so freshness banks rather than fatigue.

briefing.purpose: Endurance — time on feet grows capillaries, fat metabolism and durability. Unstructured on purpose: no targets, run to feel, switch off.
briefing.feel: Relaxed, conversational. The watch stays quiet today — that's the point.
briefing.if_wrong: Fading late is normal early in a plan; walk breaks beat abandoning. Feeling great ≠ speed up — save it for the structured long runs.
briefing.cue: Check posture every ~15min: tall hips, relaxed shoulders, quiet feet.

weeks.intro: Cutback week (Taper phase) — volume drops on purpose. Adaptation happens in the recovery, not the work; resist making up the kilometres, next week builds from a higher base because of this one.

workouts.name: RACE DAY — Half Marathon
workouts.description: RACE DAY — Half Marathon
workouts.notes: Race day. Your recent easy pace has sat ~4:57/km and your marathon-pace sessions have held 4:16-4:32/km under control — trust the paces this plan has built toward rather than the adrenaline of the start line.

briefing.purpose: The day it was all for. Nothing new today — the kit, fueling and pacing you rehearsed are the plan.
briefing.structure: RACE DAY — Half Marathon
briefing.feel: First third controlled (it should feel too easy), middle third rhythmic, final third everything you have left.
briefing.if_wrong: Bad patch mid-race? They pass — ease 5 s/km for 2 minutes, take fuel, rebuild. Never surge to 'make up' time.
briefing.fuel: Race-day intake exactly as rehearsed on the long runs.

weeks.intro: Race week. The work is banked — nothing you do now makes you fitter, plenty can make you tired. Short, sharp, rested.

rationale: Built for a Half Marathon on 2026-09-20 off a Garmin VO2 Max of 53.4 (vdot-derived paces: easy 4:35-5:03/km, marathon 4:16-4:32/km, threshold 4:04-4:18/km) and a training_status of Recovery. Your logged running mileage sits around 13.5km/week, well below what a half marathon normally asks for, but your Garmin 7-day training load (~480-500) is high because of near-daily HYROX/cardio cross-training — so the Base phase ramps run volume conservatively (14.4 to 18.2km/week) before Build and Peak push toward 29.3km/week, rather than assuming a blank aerobic slate. Two time trials (Jul 21, Aug 18) recalibrate paces mid-block since the vdot estimate is Garmin-derived rather than from a recent standalone race.
tips: Your cadence has sat 150-160 spm across recent runs (vs. a healthier 170+) — every strides/speed/VO2max session in this plan is a chance to practise quicker turnover; it's the cheapest durability upgrade available to you right now.

You're already absorbing ~480-500 points of weekly training load from near-daily HYROX/cardio classes even though running mileage is low — treat every 'easy' and 'long run' day here as genuinely easy, since the aerobic stress is largely coming from elsewhere.

Training readiness swung from 18 to 47 with HRV flipping Unbalanced-to-Balanced inside 48 hours around Aug 1-2 — check readiness before quality days (tempo/threshold/VO2max) rather than running purely by the calendar.
Only one run has a logged RPE so far (5/10 on the Jul 8 County Dublin run) — log RPE after sessions when you can, since that's the signal future pace recalibrations lean on.
